catalog_quote: Zum Akzentproblem bieten die Jarring'schen Texte einiges Material. J. hat sich in allen Fällen, in denen eine von der üblichen Akzentuierungsweise (prima schwächer, ultima stärker) abweichende gesprochen wurde, den Akzent besonders bezeichnet. Es muß eine Anzahl Fälle abgezogen werden, in denen der Akzent durch besondere Bildungen beeinflußt wird, wie z. B. bei der Bildung des Verbum negativum (von J. nicht besonders bezeichnet), der Verbalkompositionen und beim Antritt gewisser Suffixe an Nominalstämme; außerdem haben wir in Fremd- resp. Lehnwörtern die häufige Ersetzung von Länge durch Akzent (die umgekehrte Erscheinung haben wir in sibirischen Türk-Sprachen, wo an Stelle von fremdem [russischem] Akzent die Länge tritt). Aber in allen andern Fällen scheinen folgende Verhältnisse vorzuliegen: 1. Festen Akzent haben regelmäßig a) die direkten Interrogativa nåjergä, qájer, qájerdä etc. (passim); b) die zu Hilfsverbum resp. Suffixen gewordenen Formen von der Wz. är-/er-: -ímiš, ekán, emäs/emás, die den Akzent auch bei weiterem Antritt von Suffixen bewahren ... c) die mit betontem -dá < taγy zusammengesetzten Konjunktionen agardá, magardá, hamdá, lekindá; d) die Konjunktion faqát; e) die 2. Silbe von taráf/taráp etc. < arab. ṭaraf, auch bei Antritt von Suffixen ...

new_statements.translation: On the accent problem Jarring's texts offer some material. In all cases where an accentuation deviating from the usual one (first syllable weaker, last syllable stronger) was spoken, J. marked the accent specially. A number of cases must be set aside in which the accent is influenced by particular formations, e.g. the negative verb (not specially marked by J.), verb compounds, and the addition of certain suffixes to nominal stems ... But in all other cases the following relations seem to hold: 1. Fixed accent regularly have a) the direct interrogatives nåjergä, qájer, qájerdä etc. ...

new_statements.rule_in_words: Default word accent in the Andkhoy (Afghan) Uzbek of Jarring's informant is on the final syllable (the first syllable weaker, the ultima stronger) and normally moves to the last syllable as suffixes are added; Menges lists the lexical/morphological classes that deviate from this.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described beyond the remark that the first syllable is 'weaker' than the ultima.
new_statements.exceptions: pp. 681-682: fixed non-final accent on interrogatives (qájer, nåjergä), copular ékan/émas/-ímiš (kept under further suffixation: ekánin, ekánligini), conjunctions with stressed enclitic -dá (agardá, magardá, hamdá, lekindá), faqát, taráf/taráp (tarápka, taráfindan); 3sg perfect frequently accented on the syllable before -di (čiqíšti, korsátti); sporadic accent before gerund -ip (tuzálip); some nouns keep accent on the last stem syllable when suffixed (qišlóqda, aјáγidan, čirájliq, albásti); 1sg imperative tanitúrajin and periphrastic jurárdi; šahár always on 2nd syllable; loans where accent stands for original length or precedes a geminate/cluster (tamåša, mujássar, daráxlar, afándi); accent before enclitic -dá in qačándä; negative verb forms (not marked by Jarring).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level accent as transcribed in dictated narrative texts from one 32-year-old male speaker from Andkhoy (Andkhui), Faryab, NW Afghanistan, recorded by Jarring in Kabul 1935; Menges' statement is an analysis of Jarring's accent marks, not of his own field data.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement concerns the Uzbek of Andkhoy (Andkhui), Faryab province, NW Afghanistan — Jarring's single informant Osman (b. c. 1903), an urban, heavily Iranised, vowel-harmony-less y-dialect (Polivanov's 'iranized' group per Jarring p. III; Menges p. 675). This falls under Glottolog sout2699 Southern Uzbek [uzs]; it is not representative of the Qypchaq (j-) 'Real Uzbek', Moγol or Qoŋurat dialects of NE Afghanistan described by Baldauf 2011. Menges' rule is a second-order analysis of Jarring's printed accent marks rather than of Menges' own recordings, hence confidence medium; the reading (final default + listed pre-stressing/lexical exceptions) matches what the catalog holds for Northern Uzbek (nort2690: Kononov 1960, Sjoberg 1963).

sources.note: Only a marking convention (glossary preface p. [169], PDF p. 177): 'The stress accent is marked by the sign ˈ placed before the vowel of the syllable on which it falls.' Brief 'Remarks on the dialect' (p. III) treat vowels/vowel harmony only; no stress rule stated. About 40 glossary headwords carry the mark (af'andi, tar'af, fag'at, qar'a..), i.e. marking is selective; the promised Andkhui grammar never appeared.
